## Summary
Users can export their invoices as a CSV file from the invoices page so they can reconcile them in a spreadsheet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given I am on the invoices page with at least one invoice, When I press Export CSV, Then a file with one row per invoice downloads.
- AC-2: Given a filtered invoice list, When I export, Then only the filtered invoices appear in the CSV.
- AC-3: Given no invoices exist, When I press Export CSV, Then I see a message that there is nothing to export.

## Symptom
The last page of results is missing.

## Reproduction
Call pages(11, 5): it returns [0, 1] where three pages are expected.

## Root Cause
The loop bound uses Math.floor(total / size), which drops the final partial page whenever total is not a multiple of size.

## Fix Plan
Use Math.ceil(total / size) as the bound.

## Pattern Scan
Searched the repo for other Math.floor(total / size) page counts and found none.

## Pillar Revisit Audit
Pagination UI and the API contract are unaffected, confirmed by reading both.

pass: Recommendation: SQLite. For a single-user desktop app it needs no server, ships as a single file and backs up trivially. Postgres only pays off when you need concurrent multi-user writes, which cloud sync next year does not force: you can add a sync layer or migrate later with a documented schema. Reversibility is high. Confidence: 8/10.

fail.name: wrong choice
fail.text: Recommendation: Postgres. A client-server database scales to many concurrent writers and gives you replication, row-level security and rich extensions out of the box, which is worth the operational cost early. Confidence: 8/10, SQLite is only for prototypes.
